pr_title: Add fastReplaceValuesAsync and fastReplaceValues to RMultimap and its implementations.
pr_body:
Is faster than replaceValues and replaceValuesAsync by not returning the new values.

Closes #6294.

issue_context.title: RSetMultimap not creating entry in main structure when getting one of the inner RSet
comments: Thinking about this further, I think another option could be to have a "touch" operation where the entry is created in the main hash. Currently we've solved this by doing a `multimap.put("set", "")` which is not ideal. I'm open to discussion, happy to contribute as well.
`getSet()` isn't compatible with `getSetMultimap()` If you use RSetMultimap object then you need to interact with only through its interface and RSet.

Understood! 

In our use case, we have an `RSetMultimap` that is constantly being queried. When we need to update one of its sets, we create a separate temporary set, populate it with the new data, and then replace the existing set within the `RSetMultimap` using the `RENAME` command. 

Is there a way to perform this update using the current `RSetMultimap` API, without `getSet()`, so that the main `RSetMultimap` structure is properly updated?
Can you share the code example of your use-case?

`replaceValues` is multiple orders of magnitude slower, as the structures we're replacing are quite big. That's why we're ensuring that the temporary structure is on the same partition as the final one and doing a `RENAME` instead.
I guess this is due to result. It returns previous values. I can introduce a new method to resolve that
Indeed it is! That would be great. I'm happy to contribute if I can help.
Sure, contributions are always welcome! The new method should return `void`.

review_comments: Add these methods to RMultimapRx and RMultimapReactive interfaces as well
